## What is an automatic bid? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-an-automatic-bid)

What is an automatic bid?
An automatic bid is a guaranteed tournament spot. Win your conference tournament, and you are in. No committee vote can take it away.
Visual: Bar showing the 68-team field: 32 automatic bids and 36 at-large bids.
One spot for every conference
Division I has 32 conferences, NCAA.com says.
Each conference holds its own tournament.
It comes after the regular season ends.
Win that tournament, and you are in.
Your regular-season record does not matter here.
A losing season can still end here.
One hot week can save a season.
The sure thing, and its flip side
This is the only sure way in.
No ranking has to approve you.
No committee has to choose you.
The flip side cuts the other way.
A great team can lose its final.
Then it must wait on the committee.
It hopes for an
at-large bid
instead.
Automatic bids in the field
The 2027 field holds 68 teams.
NCAA.com calls each winner an automatic qualifier.
Every other spot goes to at-large teams.
The four lowest-seeded automatic qualifiers play early.
They play two First Four games.
They face only other automatic qualifiers there.
Read
how the First Four works
.
Why your bracket cares
These winners fill many small-conference spots.
Some arrive with losing records.
Some arrive red hot in March.
In 2027, it is Sunday, March 14.

Common questions
What is an automatic bid?
An automatic bid is the March Madness spot a team earns by winning its conference tournament. Every Division I conference tournament winner gets one, whatever its regular-season record was. The selection committee does not choose these teams.
Can a team with a losing record get an automatic bid?
Yes. NCAA.com says the winner earns the trip regardless of regular-season performance. Win the conference tournament, and the spot is yours, even after a losing regular season.

## What is an at-large bid? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-an-at-large-bid)

What is an at-large bid?
An at-large bid is the committee's own invitation. The team did not win its conference tournament. The committee still judged its season strong enough.
Visual: Bar showing the 68-team field: 32 automatic bids and 36 at-large bids.
The second way into the field
Teams reach March Madness two ways.
One way is winning your conference tournament.
That earns an
automatic bid
, no questions asked.
You lost your conference tournament final.
Or you fell short even earlier.
The committee can still pick you.
It picks the strongest seasons left.
Who hands these bids out
A selection committee makes every pick.
There are separate men's and women's committees.
Members cannot vote for their own teams.
The committee works in three phases.
First it selects the at-large teams.
Then it seeds all 68 teams.
Then it places them in the bracket.
Read
what a seed is
.
What the committee looks at
NCAA.com names the tools members use.
They include the NET rankings.
They include one-page team sheets.
Team sheets show strength of schedule.
They show quality wins and losses.
They show head-to-head results too.
They show the road record too.
No single ranking decides a pick.
The committee weighs the whole season.
No limit from one conference
Each conference gets one automatic bid.
At-large bids have no such limit.
The committee may pick several per conference.
Strong leagues often send many teams.
In 2027, the lowest four play early.
They play two First Four games.
They face only other at-large teams there.
The last picks learn last, on Sunday.
Those teams sit
on the bubble
all week.

Common questions
What is an at-large bid?
An at-large bid is a March Madness invitation the selection committee gives a team that did not win its conference tournament. The committee judges the team's whole season strong enough to earn one of the spots the automatic bids do not fill.
How many at-large bids are there?
There are 36 at-large bids. The full field holds 68 teams. Automatic bids fill 32 spots first.

## What is a bubble team? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-bubble-team)

What is a bubble team?
A bubble team could make the field, or miss it. It did not win its conference tournament. Its whole season sits on the cut line.
Visual: Bar showing the 68-team field: 32 automatic bids and 36 at-large bids.
On the bubble, in plain words
Qualification could go either way.
The team sits on the verge.
An invitation is not guaranteed.
It is not an official label.
The committee never uses the term.
Fans and broadcasts use it instead.
Waiting on the last at-large bids
It needs an
at-large bid
from the committee.
Only the final few bids remain.
Many similar seasons chase them.
The last four picked are celebrated.

The next four are left out.
Fans call them the first four out.
NCAA.com says they top the NIT field.
Bid stealers shrink the bubble

Common questions
What is a bubble team?
A bubble team is a team on the edge of the March Madness field. It did not win its conference tournament, so it needs one of the last at-large bids from the selection committee, and its qualification could go either way.
What does on the bubble mean?
It means the team is on the verge of making the field, but an invitation is not guaranteed. The last four at-large teams picked are called the last four in, and the first teams left out are called the first four out.

## What is bracketology? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-bracketology)

What is bracketology?
Bracketology is predicting the tournament before it exists. Fans and analysts guess the whole field. They guess every seed too.
Visual: Bracketology timeline: the word appears in 1996, predictors publish mock brackets all season, and the real field replaces every projection on Selection Sunday.
A made-up science, proudly
NCAA.com gives the plain definition.
It is predicting the tournament field.
It is predicting every team's seed.
Some predictors also pick game winners.
The word itself is made up.
NCAA.com calls it a made-up ology.
It jokes: do not change majors.
The man who named it
Reports credit ESPN analyst Joe Lunardi.
He called himself a bracketologist first.
The Philadelphia Inquirer printed it in 1996.
His ESPN projections followed that year.
Fans now call him Joey Brackets.
He still updates brackets all season.
Dozens of rivals now publish theirs too.
What a bracketologist actually does
The job is mimicking the committee.
Predictors study the same team sheets.
They weigh quality wins and losses.
They watch the NET rankings closely.
They track
bubble teams
every week.
Every update is a mock bracket.
It ends with the last four in.
NCAA.com runs its own predictions too.
Andy Katz files them all season.
His final 2019 prediction scored 67.
Just one picked team missed out.
Bracketology in the 68-team era
Some talk says the field may grow.
The 2027 field holds 68 teams.
No change has been decided.
Any change is the NCAA's call.
Every projection still dies on Sunday.
The committee reveals the real field then.
Check the
Selection Sunday 2027
date.

Common questions
What is bracketology?
Bracketology is the practice of predicting which teams make the NCAA tournament field and how they are seeded, and sometimes who wins each game. NCAA.com calls it a made-up ology. The field being predicted holds 68 teams.
Who invented bracketology?
Reports credit ESPN analyst Joe Lunardi. The word bracketologist appeared beside his name in The Philadelphia Inquirer in February 1996, and his bracket projections reached ESPN the same year. NCAA.com's own predictor is Andy Katz, whose final 2019 prediction named 67 of the 68 teams in the field.

## How many rounds are in March Madness? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-many-rounds-are-in-march-madness)

Count seven stages in 2027. The First Four comes first. Six rounds follow in the main bracket.

Common questions
How many rounds are in March Madness?
In 2027 there are seven stages: the First Four, then the First Round, Second Round, Sweet 16, Elite Eight, Final Four, and the championship game. The main bracket that fans pick holds six of those rounds, starting with 64 teams.
How many games must a team win to be champion?
A team that starts in the main bracket must win six straight games. A team that starts in the First Four must win seven straight, because it has to win its way into the main bracket first.

## What is the NIT? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-nit)

What is the NIT?
The NIT is postseason basketball's second stage. Strong teams miss March Madness yearly. The NIT invites the best of them.
Visual: Bar showing the 100 postseason spots in 2027: 68 in the NCAA tournament and 32 in the NIT.
The full name says it
NIT stands for National Invitation Tournament.
Invitations decide the whole field here.
Its field forms on Selection Sunday.
The NCAA field is announced first.
The NIT field follows the same day.
Both fields appear Sunday, March 14, 2027.
Older than March Madness itself
The NIT began in 1938.
The NCAA tournament began in 1939.
NCAA.com calls it the oldest postseason event.
It was once the top prize.
The NCAA runs it today.
The 2027 edition is its 89th.
Its champion earns no national title.
Who gets invited in 2027
The 2027 field holds 32 teams.
The NCAA field holds 68 teams.
A bigger NCAA field has been talked about.
No change has been decided.
Total postseason spots add up to 100.
The first four out headline it.
Meet the
bubble teams
behind that phrase.
Those four become No. 1 seeds.
Regular-season champions earn automatic bids too.
Their rankings must average 125 or better.
Ten top conferences get exempt bids.
The ACC and SEC get extras.
Teams may decline an invitation.
How the 2027 NIT is played
Early rounds play on campus sites.
The first round holds eight games.
Winners then face the top eight seeds.
Semifinals land Tuesday, March 30, on campus.
The final shares Final Four weekend.
Detroit Mercy hosts it Sunday, April 4.
The men's title game follows Monday.
ESPN airs every NIT game.
Read about the
Final Four
weekend.
Five questions start your bracket. Your picks finish it.
Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
What is the NIT?
The NIT is the National Invitation Tournament, a single-elimination postseason tournament run by the NCAA for teams that miss the NCAA tournament field. In 2027 it holds 32 teams, and its champion is crowned at Detroit Mercy on Sunday, April 4.
Is the NIT the same as March Madness?
No. March Madness is the NCAA tournament, which crowns the national champion. The NIT is a separate tournament for the strongest teams left out, including the first four out of the NCAA field, who enter as No. 1 seeds.

## What is a conference tournament? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-conference-tournament)

What is a conference tournament?
A conference tournament is each league's own playoff. Every league holds one after the season. Its winner earns an automatic bid.
Visual: Bar showing the 68-team field: 32 automatic bids and 36 at-large bids.
Thirty-two leagues hold one
Division I holds 32 conferences.
Each conference runs its own tournament.
It starts after the regular season ends.
That team also leaves with a bid.
The prize is automatic

Common questions
What is a conference tournament?
A conference tournament is the postseason tournament each of the 32 Division I conferences holds after the regular season. The winner earns an automatic bid to the NCAA tournament, no matter how its regular season went.
Does the regular-season champion get the automatic bid?
No. The automatic bid goes to the conference tournament winner, not the regular-season champion. A team can finish near the bottom of its league, win the tournament, and still reach March Madness.

## What are NET rankings? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-are-net-rankings)

What are NET rankings?
NET rankings are the committee's main sorting tool. NET stands for NCAA Evaluation Tool. It ranks teams for selection and seeding.
Visual: The four quadrants sort wins by the foe's NET rank. At home: Quadrant 1 is ranks 1 to 30, Quadrant 2 is 31 to 75, Quadrant 3 is 76 to 160, Quadrant 4 is 161 to 353.
What NET stands for
NET means NCAA Evaluation Tool.
It arrived for the 2018-19 season.
It replaced the older RPI ranking.
The RPI used only winning percentages.
The NCAA built NET with Google Cloud.
Men and women get separate lists.
Each list uses only its own games.
The two parts of the NET
Part one is the Team Value Index.
It rewards beating strong teams.
Road and neutral wins count extra.
Part two is adjusted net efficiency.
It tracks points per hundred possessions.
It adjusts for foe and place.
Winning percentage alone no longer counts.
Scoring margin no longer counts either.
No past season data sneaks in.
How the committee uses it
The NET is a sorting tool only.
It never decides the field alone.
The committee still weighs the full season.
There is no set formula for bids.
New rankings post daily in season.
The first list comes in December.
See how
at-large bids
get picked.
Quadrants sort wins by strength
Team sheets sort games into four quadrants.
Quadrant 1 holds the hardest wins.
Quadrant 4 holds the easiest games.

Common questions
What are NET rankings?
NET rankings are the NCAA Evaluation Tool rankings, the selection committee's primary sorting tool since the 2018-19 season. They combine the Team Value Index with adjusted net efficiency, and they replaced the RPI.
What is a Quad 1 win?
A Quad 1 win is a win over a top team in the NET rankings: at home against a team ranked 1 to 30, at a neutral site against 1 to 50, or on the road against 1 to 75. Quad 1 wins are the strongest wins a team can show the committee.

Common questions
What is a bid stealer?
A bid stealer is a team that would not have earned an at-large bid but wins its conference tournament and claims the automatic bid instead. Each steal leaves one fewer at-large spot for bubble teams.
What is the most famous bid stealer?
NC State in 2024. The Wolfpack won the ACC tournament to secure a bid it would not have earned at large, then made a run to the Final Four.

## What is the selection committee? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-selection-committee)

What is the selection committee?
The selection committee picks the at-large teams. It also seeds and brackets the field. Separate committees run the men's and women's tournaments.
Visual: The selection committee's three jobs: pick the at-large teams, seed all 68 teams, and place them in the bracket.
Twelve people sit on it
Each committee holds 12 members.
Members serve five-year terms.
They are conference commissioners and athletics directors.
Experienced administrators sit with them.
They come from across Division I.
Three jobs, one reveal
First, they pick the at-large teams.
Automatic qualifiers need no pick.
Next, they seed all 68 teams.
Then they place teams into brackets.
The reveal comes on Selection Sunday.
See how
at-large bids
get picked.
They watch all season long
Watching starts on the season's first night.
It runs straight through Selection Sunday.
Members meet many times each season.
Each member monitors up to six conferences.
Nobody monitors their own league.
No formula, and no home cooking
No single metric decides any pick.
Members weigh results, metrics, and observations.
The NET and
Wins Above Bubble
help.
Members cannot vote for their own school.
Every pick comes by secret ballot.
Five questions start your bracket. Your picks finish it.
Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
What is the selection committee?
The selection committee is the NCAA Division I Basketball Committee. Its 12 members pick the at-large teams, seed all 68 teams, and place them in the bracket for March Madness.
Can a committee member vote for their own school?
No. Committee members may not vote for their own school's team, and they may not monitor the league they represent. Every other pick is made by secret ballot.

## What is Wins Above Bubble? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-wins-above-bubble)

What is Wins Above Bubble?
Wins Above Bubble counts results, not style. It compares your wins with a bubble team's expected wins. Same schedule, two different totals.
Visual: Wins Above Bubble scale: below zero means behind the bubble, zero is the bubble line, above zero means ahead of the bubble.
A resume score, in wins
WAB stands for Wins Above Bubble.
Each game adds one small value.
Values run from 1 to minus 1.
Those values add into one total.
Higher totals mean stronger resumes.
The bubble team is the bar
Picture an average bubble team.
Now hand it your schedule.
Count the wins it would average.
Beat that count, and WAB rises.
Fall short, and WAB drops below zero.
Meet the
bubble teams
it measures.
Results only, never style
Margin of victory never counts.
Efficiency never counts either.
Only the final result matters.
Winning hard games lifts the score.
The NET helps judge each opponent.
Read how
NET rankings
work.
Why the committee keeps it close
NCAA.org names two common computer metrics.
They are the NET and WAB.
The NET measures efficiency and strength.
WAB measures what actually happened.
No single metric decides a bid.
See who weighs them: the
selection committee
.
Five questions start your bracket. Your picks finish it.
Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
What is Wins Above Bubble?
Wins Above Bubble, or WAB, is a results-based metric that shows how many more or fewer wins a team earned than a bubble team would average against the same schedule. The NCAA committees use it beside the NET rankings.
What is the difference between WAB and NET?
The NET is a predictive metric based on efficiency and opponent strength. WAB is a results metric: it ignores margin and efficiency, and counts only what a team actually won against its schedule.

## How to fill out a March Madness bracket (https://fillmybracket.com/how-to-fill-out-a-march-madness-bracket)

How to fill out a March Madness bracket
Wait for Selection Sunday, when the teams are announced. Then pick a winner for every game, round by round, until one champion is left. That is the whole job.
Visual: The five steps: wait for the field, pick round one, keep picking winners, end with one champion, hand it in on time.
Step 1: Wait for the field
Brackets open on Selection Sunday. In 2027, that is Sunday, March 14. The teams and matchups are announced that evening.
Step 2: Pick the first round
The main bracket starts with 32 games. Pick one winner in each game. Not sure? Trust the seeds. A low seed number means a strong team. Seed 1 is the strongest. Seed 16 is the weakest.
Step 3: Keep picking winners
Every winner moves on to the next round. Your picks play each other in round two. Keep going through the Sweet 16 and the Elite Eight.
Step 4: End with one champion
Four teams reach the Final Four. Pick two winners, then pick the final. Some pools also ask for a tiebreaker. That is a guess at the total points in the final game.
Step 5: Hand it in on time
Pools lock when the first round starts. In 2027, the first round starts Thursday, March 18. A late bracket counts for nothing. Finish before Thursday morning.
Three tips that hold up
Do not send all four 1 seeds to the Final Four. It has happened twice: in 2008 and in 2025.
Pick a few upsets early. Low seeds win about one first-round game in four.
Keep your champion safe. Most champions are 1 or 2 seeds.
Five questions start your bracket. Your picks finish it.
Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
How do you fill out a March Madness bracket?
Wait for Selection Sunday, when the teams are announced. Then pick a winner for every game, round by round, until one champion is left. Pools lock before the first main-round games, so hand it in on time.
When do I need to finish my bracket?
Before the first round starts. In 2027 that is Thursday, March 18. Most pools lock at the tip of the first game that day.

## What is a March Madness bracket? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-march-madness-bracket)

What is a March Madness bracket?
A bracket is the chart of the whole NCAA basketball tournament. It lists every game. You fill it in by picking the winner of each game, round by round, until one champion is left.
Visual: The main bracket shrinks round by round: 64 teams, then 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, and one champion across 63 games.
Why it is called March Madness
The tournament runs for three weeks in March. Upsets happen almost every day. Big teams fall early. Small schools win games nobody saw coming.
How the chart works
Teams are split into four regions. Each region has 16 teams. Every team gets a seed, a rank from 1 to 16. Seed 1 is the strongest. Seed 16 is the weakest. First games pair a high seed with a low seed. Lose once and you go home. Win and you move one step right on the chart.
How many games?
The main bracket has 63 games. 32 games in the first round. Then 16, then 8, then 4. The last four teams are the Final Four. Two more games leave one champion. The tournament holds 68 teams.
Why people fill one out
Friends, families, and offices run pools. Everyone fills in a bracket. The best score wins the pool. Most players know very little basketball.
Five questions start your bracket. Your picks finish it.
Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
What is a March Madness bracket?
A bracket is the chart of the whole NCAA basketball tournament. It lists every game. You fill it in by picking the winner of each game, round by round, until one champion is left.
How many games are in a March Madness bracket?
The main bracket has 63 games: 32 in the first round, then 16, 8, 4, 2, and the final. The tournament starts with 68 teams, and the First Four trims the field to 64 before the main bracket begins.

## How does bracket scoring work? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-does-bracket-scoring-work)

How does bracket scoring work?
You earn points for every pick you get right. Later rounds are worth more points. The highest total after the title game wins the pool.
Visual: Points per right pick double each round: 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, then 320 for the title game. A perfect bracket scores 1,920 points.
One common system
Many big pools use these points. First round: 10 points per right pick, 32 games. Second round: 20, 16 games. Sweet 16: 40, 8 games. Elite Eight: 80, 4 games. Final Four: 160, 2 games. Title game: 320, 1 game.
A perfect bracket scores 1,920 points in this system. The longest known run got 49 picks right in a row, in 2019.
Why late rounds rule
One right champion pick earns 320 points. That equals 32 right picks in the first round. The pool is won in the last two rounds. Guard your Final Four picks with care.
Every pool sets its own rules
Some pools use 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 points. Some give bonus points when a low seed wins. Ask how your pool scores before you pick. Most pools also ask for a tiebreaker. Guess the total points scored in the title game. Closest guess wins a tie.
Five questions start your bracket. Your picks finish it.
Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
How does bracket scoring work?
You earn points for every pick you get right. Later rounds are worth more points. In one common system, a right pick earns 10 points in the first round, then 20, 40, 80, 160, and 320 for the final. The highest total after the title game wins the pool.
How many points is a perfect bracket worth?
In the common 10-20-40-80-160-320 system, a perfect bracket scores 1,920 points. No one has ever picked a perfect bracket to the end.

## What is a Cinderella team? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-cinderella-team)

What is a Cinderella team?
A Cinderella is a team nobody expected to win. It is a low seed that beats big teams and stays alive late into the tournament.
Visual: Saint Peter's in 2022: a 15 seed that beat Kentucky, a 2 seed, then beat Purdue and reached the Elite Eight, the first 15 seed ever to get that far.
Why the fairy tale name?
The name comes from the Cinderella story. A girl in rags shows up at the ball. A small school with a low seed does the same.
Famous Cinderellas
Saint Peter's, 2022. A 15 seed from a tiny school. They beat Kentucky, a 2 seed, in the first round. Then they beat Purdue and reached the Elite Eight. No 15 seed had ever gone that far.
Villanova, 1985. An 8 seed that won the whole thing. They beat Georgetown in the final, 66 to 64. No seed lower than 8 has ever won the title.
Loyola Chicago, 2018. An 11 seed in the Final Four.
Florida Gulf Coast, 2013. The first 15 seed to reach the Sweet 16.
Why Cinderellas wreck brackets
One Cinderella run busts all those picks at once. Almost every year, a team seeded 10 or worse reaches the Sweet 16. The art is picking one or two, not ten.

Common questions
What is a Cinderella team in March Madness?
A Cinderella is a low seed that nobody expected to win, which beats strong teams and stays alive late into the tournament. The name comes from the fairy tale: a team in rags shows up at the ball and steals the night.
What is the lowest seed to win March Madness?
A number 8 seed. Villanova won the title in 1985. No seed lower than 8 has ever won the championship.

## When is Selection Sunday 2027? (https://fillmybracket.com/when-is-selection-sunday-2027)

When is Selection Sunday 2027?
Selection Sunday is Sunday, March 14, 2027. The full field is announced on TV that evening. Brackets open right after the show.
Visual: The 2027 dates that matter: Selection Sunday March 14, First Four March 16 and 17, First Round March 18 and 19, Final Four April 3, title game April 5.
What happens that night
A committee names every team in the tournament. Each team learns its seed and its first game. You have about three days before the first round.
The 2027 dates that matter
Selection Sunday: Sunday, March 14. First Four (4 games): Tuesday and Wednesday, March 16-17. First round: Thursday and Friday, March 18-19. Second round: Saturday and Sunday, March 20-21. Sweet 16: Thursday and Friday, March 25-26. Elite Eight: Saturday and Sunday, March 27-28. Final Four, in Detroit: Saturday, April 3. Title game, in Detroit: Monday, April 5.
The women's tournament shares Selection Sunday. Its Final Four is April 2 and 4, in Columbus.
The field in 2027
The field holds 68 teams. Four First Four games trim the field to 64.
When to fill in your bracket
Start on Sunday night, March 14. Pools lock before the first round starts. That is the morning of Thursday, March 18.

## How often do upsets happen? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-do-upsets-happen)

How often do upsets happen in March Madness?
Every year. Since 1985, the lower seed has won about one first-round game in four. Picking all favorites is not the safe play it looks like.
Visual: First-round upset rates since 1985: 9 seeds beat 8 seeds 52 times in 100, 10 seeds beat 7 seeds 39 times in 100, 11 over 6 is 39, 12 over 5 is 36, 13 over 4 is 21, 14 over 3 is 14, 15 over 2 is 7, 16 over 1 is 1.
The first-round seed math, since 1985
12 seed vs 5 seed: 58 wins in 164 games. 11 seed vs 6 seed: 64 wins in 164 games. 10 seed vs 7 seed: 63 wins in 164 games. 13 seed vs 4 seed: 33 wins in 164 games. 14 seed vs 3 seed: 23 wins in 164 games. 15 seed vs 2 seed: 11 wins in 164 games. 16 seed vs 1 seed: 2 wins in 164 games.
The 12-over-5 upset is the famous one. The 8-vs-9 game is a coin flip. In fact, 9 seeds win it a bit more than half the time. We counted every game ourselves. All 2,583 men's tournament games, 1985 to 2026. First Four games are not counted. Every rate here starts at the round of 64. The full chart: which first-round upsets happen most.
The two wins nobody forgets
A 16 seed has beaten a 1 seed twice. UMBC beat Virginia in 2018. Fairleigh Dickinson beat Purdue in 2023. 164 tries. Two wins.
What happens late
Upsets thin out as rounds go on. Since 1985, 1 seeds have won more titles than all other seeds put together. A 5 seed has reached the Final Four nine times. No 5 seed has ever won the title. The lowest seed to win it all is 8.
What this means for your picks
Take one or two 12 seeds and an 11 seed in round one. Treat 8 vs 9 as a guess. History gives no real edge. Keep your champion safe. Pick a 1 or 2 seed to win it all.
History is a guide, not a promise.

How often do upsets happen in March Madness?

Has a 16 seed ever beaten a 1 seed?
Yes, twice. UMBC beat Virginia in 2018, and Fairleigh Dickinson beat Purdue in 2023. In 164 tries, those are the only two.

## What is a seed in March Madness? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-seed-in-march-madness)

What is a seed in March Madness?
A seed is a team's rank inside its region. Seed 1 is the strongest team there. Seed 16 is the weakest.
Visual: The eight first-round pairings in a region: 1 seed against 16, 2 against 15, 3 against 14, 4 against 13, 5 against 12, 6 against 11, 7 against 10, 8 against 9. Every pair adds up to 17.
Who sets the seeds?
A committee ranks the teams before the tournament starts. It splits the field into four regions. Each region gets seeds 1 through 16. In 2027, the tournament starts with 68 teams. The First Four trims the field to 64 first.
How the first round pairs up
First-round games pair seeds that add up to 17. 1 seed vs 16 seed: best team vs weakest team. 2 seed vs 15 seed: same idea, one step closer. 3 seed vs 14 seed: strong favorite. 4 seed vs 13 seed: strong favorite. 5 seed vs 12 seed: the famous upset game. 6 seed vs 11 seed: favorite, but not by much. 7 seed vs 10 seed: nearly even. 8 seed vs 9 seed: a coin flip.
A worked example, from our picker
Our picker scores every team by seed strength. A 1 seed starts at 32. A 16 seed starts at 2. So a 5 seed starts at 24, and a 12 seed starts at 10. The favorite starts 14 points ahead in that game. Your answers can still flip it. That is the fun part.
A seed is a rank, not a promise
Since 1985, the lower seed has won about one first-round game in four. The lowest seed to win the title is 8. That was Villanova, in 1985.

Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
What is a seed in March Madness?
A seed is a team's rank inside its region, from 1 to 16. A committee ranks every team before the tournament starts. Seed 1 is the strongest team in the region, and seed 16 is the weakest.
Why does a 1 seed play a 16 seed first?
To reward the best teams and save the big games for late. First-round games pair seeds that add up to 17: 1 plays 16, 2 plays 15, and so on. A 1 seed has beaten a 16 seed in all but two of 164 tries.

## How to pick upsets (https://fillmybracket.com/how-to-pick-upsets)

How to pick upsets in March Madness
Pick a few, in the right spots. About one first-round game in four is an upset, and most of them live in the same few matchups.
Visual: First-round upset rates since 1985: 10 seeds beat 7 seeds 39 times in 100, 11 over 6 is 39, 12 over 5 is 36.
Five rules, from the seed math
Start with the 12-over-5 game. It hits about 35 times in 100. Add an 11 seed over a 6 seed. About 39 in 100, since 1985. Take two or three first-round upsets. That matches history without betting the bracket. Stop before the late rounds. Favorites rule late. Keep your champion a 1 or 2 seed. Never spend a pick on 16 over 1. Twice, ever, in 164 tries. Treat the 8-vs-9 game as a coin flip, not an upset. One low seed in your Sweet 16 is normal. Two is a story.
A worked example
Say you take two 12 seeds and one 11 seed. Each pick hits about 36 to 39 times in 100. Together, the chance at least one lands is about 3 in 4. Your other 29 first-round picks can stay safe. One landed upset beats every all-favorite bracket on that game.
How our picker does it
Our picker scores every team by seed strength. A 5 seed starts at 24. A 12 seed starts at 10. Your chaos answer hands the lower seed a bonus. Turn chaos up, and the 12 seed can pass the 5. Turn it down, and the favorite holds.

Common questions
How many upsets should I pick in my bracket?
Two or three in the first round is the normal range. Since 1985, about one first-round game in four is an upset, but they cluster in a few matchups, like the 12 seed against the 5 seed.
Should I pick a 16 seed to beat a 1 seed?
History says no. A 16 seed has beaten a 1 seed twice in 164 tries: UMBC in 2018 and Fairleigh Dickinson in 2023. It is a fun pick that almost always costs you a game.

## Which first-round upsets happen most often? (https://fillmybracket.com/which-first-round-upsets-happen-most)

Which first-round upsets happen most often?
The close ones. Lower seeds won 341 of 1,312 first-round games since 1985. That is about one game in four. The 10, 11, and 12 seeds do most of the damage.
Visual: First-round upset rates, men's tournament, 1985 to 2026: 9 seeds beat 8 seeds 87 times in 164, 10 over 7 is 63 in 164, 11 over 6 is 64 in 164, 12 over 5 is 58 in 164, 13 over 4 is 33 in 164, 14 over 3 is 23 in 164, 15 over 2 is 11 in 164, 16 over 1 is 2 in 164.
The full count, 1985 to 2026
9 seed vs 8 seed: 87 wins in 164 games. 10 seed vs 7 seed: 63 wins in 164 games. 11 seed vs 6 seed: 64 wins in 164 games. 12 seed vs 5 seed: 58 wins in 164 games. 13 seed vs 4 seed: 33 wins in 164 games. 14 seed vs 3 seed: 23 wins in 164 games. 15 seed vs 2 seed: 11 wins in 164 games. 16 seed vs 1 seed: 2 wins in 164 games.
The 8-vs-9 game sits at the top. Nine seeds win it a bit more than half the time. Most brackets treat it as a coin flip. History agrees.
The patterns behind the numbers
A normal year has about eight first-round upsets. The quietest year had 3. The wildest had 13. A double-digit seed reaches the Sweet 16 almost every year. It has happened in 39 of 41 tournaments, and 18 years in a row. The 11 seed is better than its number lately. Since 2013, 11 seeds have won half of their first-round games. Middle seeds can win twice. Of the 11 seeds that won in round one, 28 of 64 also won their next game. The top still rules late. One seeds have won 27 of the 41 titles since 1985.
What about the field in 2027?
The 2027 tournament holds 68 teams. Four First Four games come first. The winners join the same 64-team main bracket. These numbers count the main bracket only. Every rate starts at the round of 64.
How we counted
We counted every men's tournament game from 1985 to 2026. That is 41 tournaments and 2,583 games. There was no tournament in 2020. Game results come from the public game-by-game record. Wikipedia tournament pages, compiled in the march-madness-games-csv dataset. History is a guide, not a promise.

## How often does a 12 seed beat a 5 seed? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-12-seed-beat-a-5-seed)

How often does a 12 seed beat a 5 seed?
About 35 times in 100. The 12 seed has beaten the 5 seed 58 times in 164 games since 1985. It is the most famous upset in the bracket, and the math backs it up.
Visual: The 12-over-5 upset, by era: 18 of 60 games from 1985 to 1999, 20 of 52 from 2000 to 2012, 20 of 52 from 2013 to 2026. It has grown more common.
It happens almost every year
At least one 12 seed has won in 35 of 41 tournaments. Two won in 2025. McNeese beat Clemson. Colorado State beat Memphis. 2023 was one of the rare quiet years. No 12 seed won.
When a 12 wins, it can win again
22 of the 58 winning 12 seeds also won their next game. That is about 38 in 100. The prize is usually a beatable 4 or 13 seed. One low seed in your Sweet 16 is normal. A 12 is the classic pick.
How we counted

## How often does an 11 seed beat a 6 seed? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-an-11-seed-beat-a-6-seed)

How often does an 11 seed beat a 6 seed?
About 39 times in 100. The 11 seed has beaten the 6 seed 64 times in 164 games since 1985. Lately it is closer to a coin flip.
Visual: The 11-over-6 upset, by era: 18 of 60 games from 1985 to 1999, 20 of 52 from 2000 to 2012, 26 of 52 from 2013 to 2026. It is a coin flip now.
The recent pattern
Since 2013, 11 seeds have won 26 of 52 games against 6 seeds. That is exactly half. The early years were colder. From 1985 to 1999, 11 seeds won 18 of 60. Nobody knows one clean reason. The wins are real either way.
Eleven seeds win again, too
28 of the 64 winning 11 seeds also won their next game. That is about 44 in 100. No other upset line keeps winning like this one.
Eleven seeds go deepest
Six 11 seeds have reached the Final Four. LSU in 1986. George Mason in 2006. VCU in 2011. Loyola-Chicago in 2018. UCLA in 2021. NC State in 2024. No other double-digit seed has done it as often.

How often does a 10 seed beat a 7 seed?

## How often does a 13 seed beat a 4 seed? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-13-seed-beat-a-4-seed)

How often does a 13 seed beat a 4 seed?
About 20 times in 100. The 13 seed has beaten the 4 seed 33 times in 164 games since 1985. It happens most years, and it is still a clear step down from the 12 seed.
Visual: The 13-over-4 upset, by era: 12 of 60 games from 1985 to 1999, 12 of 52 from 2000 to 2012, 9 of 52 from 2013 to 2026. Flat for 40 years.
It still happens most years
At least one 13 seed has won in 28 of 41 tournaments. The most recent was Yale over Auburn in 2024. That is the pattern. One most years, none some years. It is a real upset. It is not close to a coin flip. The 11 seed game is closer lately: half since 2013.
These runs end fast
Only 6 of the 33 winning 13 seeds won their next game. The next game is usually against a 5 or 12 seed. Even so, about 18 in 100 of these winners reached the Sweet 16. Pick one 13 seed for fun if you like. History says one is plenty.

How is a 13-over-4 different from a 12-over-5?
It happens about half as often. The 12 seed has 57 wins since 1985. The 13 seed has 33. Both happen most years, but the 12 seed is the safer upset pick.

## What is March Madness? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-march-madness)

What is March Madness?
March Madness is the NCAA college basketball tournament. Teams play single-elimination games until one champion is left. Lose once, and your season is over.
Visual: March Madness 2027 dates: Selection Sunday March 14, First Four March 16 and 17, First Round starts March 18, Final Four April 3, title game April 5.
One loss, and you are out
The tournament crowns the national champion.
It is played every spring, mostly in March.
In 2027, 68 teams enter each tournament.
There is a men's tournament and a women's tournament.
The field is split into four regions.
Each team gets a seed, from 1 to 16.
Winners move on. Losers go home.
After the First Four, 64 teams remain.
Then come the First Round and the Second Round.
The Sweet 16, the Elite Eight, and the Final Four.
New to the chart itself? Read what a bracket is.
Where the name came from
The phrase started in Illinois high school basketball.
An official named Henry V. Porter used it in 1939.
The first NCAA tournament was also played in 1939.
CBS broadcaster Brent Musburger used the phrase on air in 1982.
He meant the NCAA tournament, and the name stuck.
Why everyone fills out a bracket
Before the games start, fans predict every winner.
That prediction sheet is the bracket.
Offices, schools, and families run pools on it.
You do not need to follow basketball to play.
Plenty of brackets are picked by mascot or by colors.
March Madness 2027, in short
The field is set on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027.
The First Four is played March 16 and 17.
The First Round starts Thursday, March 18.
The men's Final Four is Saturday, April 3, in Detroit.
The men's title game is Monday, April 5.
See every key date for 2027.

Common questions
What is March Madness?
March Madness is the NCAA Division I college basketball tournament. In 2027, 68 teams enter each tournament, men's and women's. Every game is single-elimination: lose once, and you go home. The last team standing is the national champion.
Why is it called March Madness?
An Illinois high school official, Henry V. Porter, used the phrase for basketball in 1939. CBS broadcaster Brent Musburger used it for the NCAA tournament in 1982, and the name stuck. Most of the games are played in March.
## Has anyone ever had a perfect bracket? (https://fillmybracket.com/has-anyone-ever-had-a-perfect-bracket)

Has anyone ever had a perfect bracket?
No. No one has ever turned in a verifiable perfect bracket. The best proven run is 49 straight right picks, from 2019.
Visual: No perfect bracket has ever been turned in. The longest proven streak is 49 straight right picks, from 2019. Coin-flip odds of a perfect bracket are 1 in 9.2 quintillion.
The closest anyone has come
In 2019, an Ohio man named Greg Nigl got famous.
He picked the first 49 games right, one after another.
No bracket had ever stayed perfect that long.
His run broke in the Sweet 16.
Most brackets bust in the first weekend.
Read how often upsets happen.
The math, shown
A bracket picks 63 games.
Each game has 2 possible winners.
That is 9,223,372,036,854,775,808 possible brackets.
About 9.2 quintillion. A quintillion is a billion billions.
Flip a coin for every game, and your odds are 1 in 9.2 quintillion.
Know basketball, and the odds get better, a little.
NCAA.com puts them near 1 in 120.2 billion.
You do not need perfect to win
Pools are won by good brackets, not perfect ones.
NCAA.com says pool winners average about 50 right picks.
A strong first weekend does most of the work.
So does keeping your champion alive late.

Common questions
Has anyone ever had a perfect March Madness bracket?
No. No verifiable perfect bracket has ever been turned in. The longest proven streak is 49 straight correct picks, by Greg Nigl in 2019. His bracket broke in the Sweet 16.
What are the odds of a perfect bracket?
If every game were a coin flip, the odds are 1 in 9,223,372,036,854,775,808, about 1 in 9.2 quintillion. A bracket has 63 games, so there are 2 to the 63rd power possible brackets. NCAA.com puts the odds near 1 in 120.2 billion if you know basketball.
## How to fill out a bracket if you know nothing about basketball (https://fillmybracket.com/how-to-fill-out-a-bracket-if-you-know-nothing-about-basketball)

How to fill out a bracket if you know nothing about basketball
You can. Pick by mascot, by colors, or by seed. Every March, people who never watch basketball finish full brackets, and sometimes win the pool.
Visual: Five ways to fill out a bracket with no basketball knowledge: trust the seeds, pick by mascot, pick by colors, pick by place, or flip a coin.
Five ways that need no basketball
Trust the seeds. A low seed number means a strong team. Pick the lower number in every game. It is the safe way, and it works. New to seeds? Read what a seed is.
Pick by mascot. The fiercest animal wins. A bear beats a bird. It is as good a reason as any.
Pick by colors. Your favorite colors keep advancing. Your bracket looks great, too.
Pick by place. Back schools near you, or places you have lived. Rooting is half the fun.
Flip a coin on the close ones. The 8-vs-9 game is a true coin flip. Treat it like one.
Mix them. Seeds for most games, mascots for the rest.
Two rules that keep you in it
Take a few upsets early. Low seeds win about one first-round game in four.
The 12 seed beats the 5 seed about 35 times in 100.
Pick two or three of those, and stop there.
Read how to pick upsets.
Keep your champion safe. Champions are almost always 1 or 2 seeds.
Since 1985, 1 seeds hold more titles than all other seeds combined.
How our picker does it
Our picker asks the same kinds of questions.
Your answers start all 63 games, with a reason on each pick.
You can flip any pick you do not like.

Common questions
Can I fill out a bracket if I know nothing about basketball?
Yes. Pick by seed, by mascot, by colors, or by coin flip. None of these needs basketball knowledge, and every March they fill millions of brackets. Knowledge helps the odds a little. It is not required to play.
What is the easiest way to fill out a bracket?
Trust the seeds. In every game, pick the team with the lower seed number. Add two or three upsets in the first round, and keep a 1 or 2 seed as your champion. That is a complete, sensible bracket.
## What is the Final Four? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-final-four)

What is the Final Four?
The Final Four means four teams are left. Each one won its region in March Madness. They play two semifinal games, then one title game.
Visual: The tournament stages with the Final Four highlighted: four teams, semifinals Saturday April 3 and the title game Monday April 5, 2027, in Detroit.
Four regions, four winners
The tournament splits into four regions.
NCAA.com names them South, East, West, and Midwest.
Each region plays down to one winner.
That winner is called the regional champion.
Reaching this round takes four straight wins.
A First Four team needs five straight wins.
Each region ends with its Elite Eight game.
New to the chart? Read what a bracket is.
The last weekend of the tournament
The four teams meet in one city.
They play in one arena, on one weekend.
Two semifinal games are played on Saturday.
Then they play the title game on Monday.
NCAA.com notes both rounds share one arena.
Where the name came from
The name just counts the teams left.
Four teams remain, so it is the Final Four.
NCAA.com traces the phrase to 1975.
Writer Ed Chay used it in a Cleveland newspaper.
He wrote about Marquette in the 1974 tournament.
The NCAA took up the phrase in 1978.
It later made Final Four a registered trademark.
No other United States tournament may use it.
Teams nobody saw coming
Villanova, 1985. An 8 seed that won the title.
It is still the lowest seed to win.
George Mason, 2006. An 11 seed nobody picked.
VCU, 2011. It started in the First Four.
NCAA.com calls it the only team to do that.
Loyola Chicago, 2018. Another 11 seed made it.
Read more in what a Cinderella team is.
The Final Four in 2027
The men's semifinals are Saturday, April 3, 2027.
They are played at Ford Field in Detroit.
The men's title game is Monday, April 5.
The women's semifinals are Friday, April 2.
They are played in Columbus, Ohio.
The women's title game is Sunday, April 4.
See every key date for 2027.

Common questions
What is the Final Four?
The Final Four is the last four teams in the NCAA tournament, one winner from each of the four regions. The four teams play two semifinal games, and the winners meet in the national championship game.
When and where is the Final Four in 2027?
The men's Final Four is Saturday, April 3, 2027, at Ford Field in Detroit, with the title game on Monday, April 5. The women's Final Four is Friday, April 2, in Columbus, Ohio, with its title game on Sunday, April 4.

## How many teams are in March Madness? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-many-teams-are-in-march-madness)

How many teams are in March Madness?
Each March Madness tournament, men's and women's, holds 68 teams.
Visual: Bar showing the 68-team field: 32 automatic bids and 36 at-large bids.
The short answer
Each tournament holds 68 teams today.
A bigger field has been talked about.
No change has been decided.
Any change is the NCAA's call.
The men's field last grew in 2011.
The women's field last grew in 2022.
How 68 teams become a 64-team bracket
The main bracket still holds 64 teams.
It still has the same 63 games.
8 teams play in the First Four.
They play 4 games over two days.
The 4 winners move into the main bracket.
They join 60 teams that waited.
Read how the First Four works.
How teams get in
Every conference champion earns an automatic spot.
The selection committee picks the other teams.
Those picks are called at-large bids.
The committee also gives every team a seed.
Seeds run from 1 to 16 per region.
The whole field is named on Selection Sunday.
In 2027, that is Sunday, March 14.
New to seeds? Read what a seed is.
How the field grew
The first men's tournament had just 8 teams.
The field reached 16 teams in 1951.
It reached 64 teams in 1985.
It grew to 68 teams in 2011.
The field is still 68 teams today.
It reached 68 teams in 2022.
The women's tournament began in 1982, with 32 teams.
It holds 68 teams today too.
What this means for your bracket
Your bracket still covers the main 63 games.
Selection Sunday names the 68 teams.
Pools, scoring, and deadlines work as before.
See how bracket scoring works.

Common questions
How many teams are in March Madness?
68 teams in each tournament, men's and women's. A 4-game First Four trims the 68-team field to the 64 teams of the main bracket.
Will March Madness grow past 68 teams?
A bigger field has been talked about, but no change has been decided. Any change is the NCAA's call. The 2027 fields are set on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027.

## What is the opening round in March Madness? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-opening-round-in-march-madness)

What is the opening round in March Madness?
The opening round is the First Four. Eight teams play four games. The winners take the last spots in the main bracket.
Visual: The First Four: four lowest-seeded at-large teams and four lowest-seeded automatic qualifiers play four games, and the four winners join 60 waiting teams to make the 64-team main bracket.
The opening round is the First Four
The tournament opens with the First Four.
That is 8 teams playing 4 games.
It has run since 2011.
The field holds 68 teams.
Four games trim the field to 64.
Two games are played each day.
It is played before the main bracket.
See how many teams are in the tournament.
Who plays in it
The 8 teams come in two groups.
Four are the lowest-seeded automatic qualifiers.
Those teams won their conference tournaments.
Four are the lowest-seeded at-large teams.
The winners take the last four spots.
The other 60 teams are already in.


When and where in 2027
The men's games are Tuesday, March 16.
They end on Wednesday, March 17.
They are played in Dayton, Ohio.

The women's games start a day later.
They are played March 17 and 18.

See every key date for 2027.
What the winners get
Each winner earns a main bracket spot.
The 4 winners join 60 waiting teams.
Together they make the 64-team bracket.
The First Round starts Thursday, March 18.
In 2011, VCU started in the First Four.
It went on to reach the Final Four.
NCAA.com says no team has matched that run.
A champion from here needs seven straight wins.
Every other team needs six straight wins.
Does your pool count these games?
Most pools score only the main bracket.
Their brackets lock before the First Round.
That is Thursday morning, March 18, in 2027.
Ask your pool how it scores them.

The opening round is the First Four. Eight teams play four games, and the four winners join 60 other teams in the 64-team main bracket. The First Four has opened the tournament since 2011.

The First Four games are Tuesday, March 16 and Wednesday, March 17, 2027. The women's games are Wednesday, March 17 and Thursday, March 18.

## What is the Sweet 16? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-sweet-16)

What is the Sweet 16?
The Sweet 16 is the round with 16 teams left. It is the regional semifinal round. Win here, and you reach the Elite Eight.
Visual: The tournament stages with the Sweet 16 highlighted: sixteen teams, eight games, on March 25 and 26, 2027.
Four teams left in each region
The 64-team bracket splits into four regions.
Each region starts with 16 teams.
Two rounds cut each region to four.
NCAA.com calls this round the regional semifinals.
Every team here has won two straight games.
A First Four team has won three straight.

Common questions
What is the Sweet 16?
The Sweet 16 is the regional semifinal round of the NCAA tournament, when 16 teams remain, four in each region. Teams reach it by winning two games in the main bracket, and the winners move on to the Elite Eight.
When is the Sweet 16 in 2027?
The men's Sweet 16 is Thursday, March 25 and Friday, March 26, 2027, in San Antonio, Los Angeles, Kansas City, and New York. The women's Sweet 16 is Friday, March 26 and Saturday, March 27, in Philadelphia and Las Vegas.

## What is the Elite Eight? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-elite-eight)

What is the Elite Eight?
The Elite Eight is the round with eight teams left. Each game is a regional final. Win, and you reach the Final Four.
Visual: The tournament stages with the Elite Eight highlighted: eight teams, four regional finals, on March 27 and 28, 2027.
Two teams left in each region
The 64-team bracket splits into four regions.
The Sweet 16 cuts each region to two.
Four regions times two teams makes eight.
NCAA.com calls this round the regional finals.
Each game crowns one regional champion.
The champion moves on to the Final Four.
Every team here has won three straight games.
A First Four team has won four straight.
New to this round? Read
what the Sweet 16 is
.
The last games of the second weekend
The Sweet 16 opens the second weekend.
The Elite Eight closes that same weekend.
The men's games are Saturday and Sunday.

Four games are played across two days.
The women's games are Sunday and Monday.
In 2027, they are March 28 and 29.
The Elite Eight in 2027
The South final is Saturday, March 27.
It is played in San Antonio, Texas.
The West final is also on Saturday.
It is played in Los Angeles, California.
The Midwest final is Sunday, March 28.
It is played in Kansas City, Missouri.
The East final is also on Sunday.
It is played in New York City.
The women's finals are in Philadelphia and Las Vegas.

Read the 1-seed row and the 12-seed row together.
A 1 seed reaches the Final Four
68 times in 164
. A 12 seed reaches the Elite Eight twice, and the Final Four never.
Five seeds own the strangest line on the table:

.

The 11 seed is the best bet to win twice: 28 of its 64 winners did.
The 9 seed is the trap: it wins the coin flip, then meets a 1 seed. Only 9 of 87 won again.
Small print on the 15s: only 11 have ever won a first game, and 4 of those 11 reached the Sweet 16. One, Saint Peter's in 2022, went to the Elite Eight.
Patterns that keep repeating
The 11 seed keeps getting better.
Its first-round win rate by era:
1985–1999
18 of 60
2000–2012
20 of 52
2013–2026
26 of 52
11 seeds vs 6 seeds, by era. Since 2013 the 11 seed wins half of these games.
A Cinderella almost always shows up.
A double-digit seed reached the Sweet 16 in 39 of 41 tournaments, the last 18 in a row. A normal year has about two of them.
Somebody's 5 seed goes home early.
At least one 12 beat a 5 in 35 of 41 years. At least one 10 won in 38 of 41, and at least one 9 in 38 of 41.
The last weekend still belongs to the top.
One seeds have won 27 of 41 titles. A Final Four of all four 1 seeds has happened only twice, in 2008 and 2025.
No seed line is owed anything.
Six 11 seeds have reached the Final Four. Zero 12, 13, 14, 15, or 16 seeds ever have.
The Upset Forecast for March 2027
Forecast as of Sunday, November 1, 2026.
Basis: every number in this section is counted from 2,583 men's tournament games, 1985 to 2026. This is a living forecast. The counted shape below barely moves, but the teams standing on each line change all season, and the
rankings page
re-reads them every week.
The 2027 field does not exist yet.
Nobody honest can forecast teams in November.
But the shape of the tournament is the steadiest thing in sports, and the shape can be counted.

the full 41-year range
The average year has 8.3 first-round upsets, and the middle year has 8.

The recent game runs a little wilder: the 13 tournaments from 2013 to 2026 averaged 8.9.

And here is a typical first weekend, start to finish:
About 8 upsets on Thursday and Friday
, led by the 9, 10, and 11 lines.
About 4 or 5 more on the weekend
, as low seeds win second games.
About 2 double-digit seeds in the Sweet 16
, next to about 10 teams seeded 4 or better.
One or two 1 seeds in the Final Four
(the average is 1.66), and a champion who is most likely a 1 seed, as 27 of 41 have been.
These are history's averages, not predictions about any 2027 team.
Which teams are standing on those lines right now, and which of them the numbers doubt, is tracked on the

: the bands, the vulnerable favorites, and the Cinderella Radar, refreshed every week of the season.
The field is set on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027.
When it is, every line above turns into a real choice on a real bracket, and the choosing stays yours.
How this differs from the ratings sites
KenPom, Torvik, and the other ratings sites rate teams, and they are good at it. This page borrows one of their numbers and names it every time.
What none of them publishes is the tournament itself, counted: how many upsets a normal year holds, which seed lines bleed, what a typical first weekend looks like.
And the tools that fill in a bracket for you, in 30 seconds, for a price? That is the one thing this site will never do. The counts are on the table. The calls stay yours.
How we counted
Counted from every men's tournament game, 1985 to 2026.
Main bracket only. First Four games are not counted.
That is 41 tournaments and 2,583 games. There was no tournament in 2020.
Game results come from the public game-by-game record: Wikipedia tournament pages, compiled in the march-madness-games-csv dataset.
The 2027 tournament holds 68 teams. Four First Four games come first, and the winners join this same 64-team bracket, so the counted frame still applies.
History is a guide, not a promise.

Common questions
What does history say will happen in March 2027?
History cannot name teams, but the shape is steady: about 8 first-round upsets (the middle half of years land between 7 and 10), about 4 or 5 more upsets in the second round, and about 2 double-digit seeds in the Sweet 16. The 2027 field is not set until Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027.
What is the deepest run a low seed has ever made?
A 15 seed, Saint Peter's in 2022, reached the Elite Eight. Two 12 seeds have reached the Elite Eight. Six 11 seeds have reached the Final Four. The lowest seed ever to win the title is an 8 seed, Villanova in 1985.
Do these numbers include the First Four?
No. Every rate here counts the main bracket only, starting at the round of 64. In 2027, 4 First Four games come first, and the winners join the same 64-team bracket.

Others receiving votes: Missouri 167, Nebraska 70, Purdue 53, Ohio State 39, North Carolina 20, TCU 17, Saint Louis 13, VCU 12, Iowa 12, Virginia Tech 10, Indiana 8, Texas A&M 6, Villanova 6, Auburn 4, Marquette 3, Nevada 2, Grand Canyon 2, Utah State 2, Santa Clara 1.

What these bands become in March
November ranks are not March seeds.
The committee seeds the field on the whole season, and four months of games will shuffle this list.
But the bands rhyme with the seed lines, and the seed lines carry 41 years of counted history (
the full analysis
).
Read today's list in bands:
Ranks 1 to 4 (Florida, Duke, Illinois, UConn): the 1-seed line.
One seeds have won 27 of 41 titles and 162 of their 164 first games. The safest seat in sports, with two famous exceptions.
Ranks 5 to 8 (Arizona, Michigan State, Texas, Tennessee): the 2-seed line.
Strong, not safe: 15 seeds have beaten 2 seeds 11 times, about once every four years.
Ranks 9 to 12 (Virginia, Houston, Louisville, Arkansas): the 3-seed line.
Three seeds lose to 14 seeds about 14 times in 100.
Ranks 13 to 16 (St. John's, Miami, Gonzaga, Michigan): the 4-seed line.
The first bullseye. Four seeds lose to 13 seeds 33 times in 164, about one time in five. The reigning champion, Michigan, sits in this band today.
Ranks 17 to 20 (Kansas, Iowa State, Texas Tech, Alabama): the 5-seed line.
The most famous trap in the tournament. Five seeds lose to 12 seeds 58 times in 164, better than one time in three. And no 5 seed has ever won the title.
Ranks 21 to 25 (USC, UCLA, Kentucky, Vanderbilt, BYU): the 6 and 7 lines.
Favorites in the two most upset-heavy games after the coin flip: 6 seeds lose to 11 seeds about 39 times in 100, and 7 seeds lose to 10 seeds about 38 times in 100.
High-ranked teams the numbers doubt
Two rankings came out this fall.
The voters published theirs, the AP poll above.
The best-known free model published its own: Bart Torvik's T-Rank, an efficiency rating the NCAA itself puts on the selection committee's team sheets.
Its preseason baseline, read on November 1, 2026, ranks all 365 teams before almost any of them has played a game.
Where the model rates a ranked team far below the voters, one of the two lists is wrong.
If the model is right, that team is a favorite standing on a trap line with less under it than its rank suggests.
These are the six biggest disagreements in the Top 25:

Read this the honest way:
this is one model's preseason baseline, a projection, never a certainty.
It will be wrong about some of these teams by January.
That is why this page re-scores the list every week instead of carving it in stone.
The disagreement runs both ways:
Kansas: voters No. 17, model No. 4.
If the model is right, a top-line team is hiding in the 5-seed band today.
Nebraska: unranked, model No. 15.
The model's 15th-best team in the country did not make the voters' Top 25 at all, on 70 votes. Somebody moves toward somebody by January.
Gonzaga: voters No. 15, model No. 8.
The model likes the Zags more than the poll does, even on the 4-seed band where 13 seeds win one time in five.
Cinderella Radar: unranked teams that could surprise in March
March's 11, 12, and 13 seeds are almost never ranked in November.
They are conference champions and fighters from leagues the polls barely watch.
Count the whole first round and about eight games a year go to the lower seed. About two double-digit seeds are still standing in the Sweet 16.
So this page scores the unranked names on three signals. All three are public, and you can check every one:
Model strength.
Torvik's model rates the team in the national top 70 even though the voters left it out. Teams that play above their seed line are where upsets come from.
Poll notice.
The team received AP votes. At least a few voters thought it belonged, which separates it from the 300 or so teams nobody mentioned.
A live path.
Its league's road to March lands teams on the 10 to 14 seed lines, where the counted upset rates run from about 14 to 39 in 100.

The radar is a watch list, not a promise: most of these teams will not make the field, and the page will say so when their signals go dark.
And the famous name both lists agree on:
North Carolina
. Twenty votes, no ranking, and the model puts the Tar Heels 47th too. A giant starts the season doubted by everyone.
What this page cannot see
Plain words about the limits, because a forecast that hides them is a sales pitch:
One model, named every time.
Torvik's T-Rank is free, public, and on the committee's own team sheets. Other respected ratings sit behind paywalls, or publish nothing in November that can be checked. One model you can verify beats three we cannot.
Preseason means priors.
In November, the model is rating last season's program, returning players, and history, not games this roster has played. Its disagreements with the voters are hypotheses, and this page treats them that way.
No injuries, no roster news.
This page does not track who is hurt or who transferred. By February, that will matter more than anything printed here, and the weekly refresh will say what changed.
A rank is not a seed.
The bands rhyme with the seed lines. The committee holds the real pen, in March.
Why a bracket site keeps a rankings page
A bracket is a set of choices, and the choices start forming now.
Every Monday, this page refreshes with the new poll, restamps its date, and re-reads the bands.
By March, the teams you have been watching all winter will land on seed lines whose history you already know.
That is the whole idea here: your team, your upsets, your calls, made with the counted record open next to them.
Five questions start your bracket. Your picks finish it.
Our picker opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Five answers start your bracket. You can flip any pick. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.
Common questions
Are the November rankings the same as the March seeds?
No. The committee seeds the tournament on the whole season in March. November ranks are a starting picture. The bands rhyme with the seed lines, which is why this page reads them that way, but any team can climb or fall by March.
When does this page update?
Every week of the season. The AP poll lands on Mondays once games begin, and this page refreshes with it, with the date and source stamped at the top.
Who is the defending champion?
Michigan, which won the April 2026 title game. The Wolverines open this season at No. 16 in the preseason AP poll.
Which unranked teams could surprise in March?
A list of unranked teams picked out using three public signals: a top-70 rating in Bart Torvik's T-Rank model, votes in the AP poll, and a league path that lands teams on the 10 to 14 seed lines. It is a list to watch, not a prediction that any of them makes the field.
Why does each Top 25 rank have a small second number?
The big number is the team's AP rank. The small raised number is its rank in Bart Torvik's T-Rank model, out of 365 teams, read on November 1, 2026. Putting both in one cell shows where the voters and the model agree, and where they do not, with no tap or second table needed.
What makes a favorite 'vulnerable' on this page?
A gap: the model rates the team eight or more spots below the voters. One of the two lists is wrong. If it is the voters, that team arrives in March standing on a trap seed line with less under it than its rank suggests. The list is re-scored every week.

## Which school has won the most March Madness titles? (https://fillmybracket.com/which-school-has-won-the-most-march-madness-titles)

Fill My Bracket starts a full March Madness bracket from five questions.
Which school has won the most March Madness titles?
UCLA has won 11 titles. That is the most of any school. Kentucky is next, with 8. UCLA won seven titles in a row.
128 days until Selection Sunday, Sunday, March 14, 2027.
Start your bracket
Most titles
School | Titles | Title years
UCLA | 11 | 1964, 1965, 1967–1973, 1975, 1995
Kentucky | 8 | 1948, 1949, 1951, 1958, 1978, 1996, 1998, 2012
North Carolina | 6 | 1957, 1982, 1993, 2005, 2009, 2017
UConn | 6 | 1999, 2004, 2011, 2014, 2023, 2024
Indiana | 5 | 1940, 1953, 1976, 1981, 1987
Duke | 5 | 1991, 1992, 2001, 2010, 2015
Kansas | 4 | 1952, 1988, 2008, 2022
Villanova | 3 | 1985, 2016, 2018
Florida | 3 | 2006, 2007, 2025
The men’s tournament, 1939 to 2026.
No tournament in 2020, so 87 titles have been won.
Louisville also won in 2013. The NCAA later vacated that title.
For your picks
Big names win a lot. They do not win every year.
Virginia and Baylor each won a first title, in 2019 and 2021.

Common questions
Which school has won the most March Madness titles?
UCLA, with 11 titles. Kentucky has 8. North Carolina and UConn have 6 each.
Has any school won three titles in a row?
Yes. UCLA won seven titles in a row, from 1967 to 1973. No other school has won three in a row.

## What is the lowest seed to win March Madness? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-lowest-seed-to-win-march-madness)

Fill My Bracket starts a full March Madness bracket from five questions.
What is the lowest seed to win March Madness?
The lowest seed to win is a No. 8 seed. Villanova did it in 1985. Villanova beat Georgetown 66 to 64 in the title game.
128 days until Selection Sunday, Sunday, March 14, 2027.
Start your bracket
The lowest seeds that won
Seed | School | Year | Title game
8 | Villanova | 1985 | Beat Georgetown 66–64
7 | UConn | 2014 | Beat Kentucky 60–54
6 | NC State | 1983 | Beat Houston 54–52
6 | Kansas | 1988 | Beat Oklahoma 83–79
Seeds began in 1979. No seed lower than 8 has ever won.
46 seeded tournaments, through 2025.
Low seeds that got close
Six No. 11 seeds have reached the Final Four.
LSU in 1986. George Mason in 2006. VCU in 2011.
Loyola Chicago in 2018. UCLA in 2021. NC State in 2024.
None of them won the title.
For your picks
A low seed can make a deep run.
History says the run ends before the title.

## How often does a 16 seed beat a 1 seed? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-16-seed-beat-a-1-seed)

Fill My Bracket starts a full March Madness bracket from five questions.
How often does a 16 seed beat a 1 seed?
Twice in 164 games. UMBC beat Virginia 74–54 in 2018. Fairleigh Dickinson beat Purdue 63–58 in 2023. The other 162 tries all lost.
128 days until Selection Sunday, Sunday, March 14, 2027.
Start your bracket
1985–19990 of 60
2000–20120 of 52
2013–20262 of 52
For 33 tournaments, it never happened. Both wins are recent.
The two wins
YearWinnerBeatScore
2018UMBCVirginia74–54
2023Fairleigh DickinsonPurdue63–58
UMBC won by 20 points. It was not close.
Neither winner won again
UMBC lost its next game, to Kansas State.
Fairleigh Dickinson lost its next game, to Florida Atlantic.
No 16 seed has ever reached the Sweet 16.

## 2026 backtest: what all-chalk would have scored (https://fillmybracket.com/2026-bracket-backtest)

Fill My Bracket starts a full March Madness bracket from five questions.
2026 backtest: what all-chalk would have scored

## What is the First Four? (https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-first-four)

What is the First Four?
The First Four is the opening round of March Madness. Eight teams play four games. The four winners take the last spots in the main bracket of 64.
Who plays in the First Four
The field starts with 68 teams.
Four of the eight are the lowest-seeded at-large picks.
Four are the lowest-seeded conference champions.
The other 60 teams wait for the main bracket.
When it happens in 2027
The field is named on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027.
The First Four games are Tuesday and Wednesday, March 16 and 17.
The main bracket starts Thursday, March 18.
Does your bracket count these games
Your bracket covers the main bracket only: 63 games.
The First Four winners simply join the 64.
Is the field getting bigger
The field is 68 teams today. A bigger field has been talked about. No change has been decided. Any change is the NCAA's call.

## How does March Madness work? (https://fillmybracket.com/how-does-march-madness-work)

How does March Madness work?
68 teams enter a fixed bracket. They play single-elimination games, round by round, until one champion is left. Lose once, and your season is over.
How teams get in
32 teams get in by winning their conference tournament (an automatic bid).
The selection committee picks the other 36 teams (at-large bids) and seeds every team from 1 to 16.
The whole field is named on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027.
How the bracket runs
The field splits into four regions of 16 teams.
The First Four trims 68 teams to 64.
Each round then cuts the field in half: 64, 32, 16 (Sweet 16), 8 (Elite Eight), 4 (Final Four), 2, 1 champion.
2027 dates: First Four March 16-17, First Round March 18-19, Second Round March 20-21, Sweet 16 March 25-26, Elite Eight March 27-28, Final Four April 3, title game April 5.
How your bracket fits
You pick the winner of each of the 63 main-bracket games before the games start. You choose your champion, your Final Four, and your upsets.

## When does March Madness start? (https://fillmybracket.com/when-does-march-madness-start)

When does March Madness start?
The games start on Tuesday, March 16, 2027, with the First Four. The main bracket starts two days later, on Thursday, March 18.
The field is named on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027.
Brackets open right after the show, and pools lock before the first round starts on March 18.
The tournament runs about three weeks.
The Final Four is Saturday, April 3, 2027, in Detroit, and the title game is Monday, April 5, in Detroit.

## Has the March Madness final ever gone to overtime? (https://fillmybracket.com/has-the-march-madness-final-ever-gone-to-overtime)

Fill My Bracket starts a full March Madness bracket from five questions.
Has the March Madness final ever gone to overtime?
Yes, eight times. The last one was in 2019. Virginia beat Texas Tech. The score was 85 to 77, in overtime.

The 1957 final. North Carolina beat Kansas 54 to 53. It took three overtimes.

No seed of 12 or higher has ever done it.
The lowest seed ever to reach the Final Four is an 11 seed.
See the full list on the lowest seed to reach the Final Four page.
So close, then done
Every one of the seven lost its semifinal game.
None of them reached the title game.
No double-digit seed has ever won the title.
The lowest seed to win is an 8 seed: Villanova, in 1985.
Read about it on the lowest seed to win March Madness page.
The run usually ends a round earlier
A double-digit seed reached the Sweet 16 in 39 of 41 tournaments.
The Final Four is a different wall.
Only seven teams in 41 years got through it.
See the counted record in the full upset analysis , and the first-round spots in how to pick upsets .
How we counted
Counted from the site’s tournament record, 1985 to 2026.
That is 41 tournaments. There was no tournament in 2020.

Common questions
How often does a double-digit seed make the Final Four?
Seven times in 41 tournaments since 1985. Six were 11 seeds, and one was a 10 seed, Syracuse in 2016.
Has a double-digit seed ever won March Madness?
No. The lowest seed to win is an 8 seed, Villanova in 1985. None of the seven double-digit Final Four teams reached the title game.
What is the lowest seed to reach the Final Four?
An 11 seed. Six 11 seeds have done it, most recently NC State in 2024.
